evidence: Wheel METADATA and console_scripts identify travis234 = travis.cli:main. The entrypoint runs the interactive coding agent.
All 488 hashed wheel RECORD entries verified. No .pth/sitecustomize/usercustomize hooks, native executable members or pyc members are present. RECORD consistency is not a trust signature.

orchestrate.py implements bounded local worker orchestration with SQLite state, Unix sockets, capability hashing and hmac.compare_digest authorization. Subprocess execution is part of the documented agent function.

No concrete stealing, backdoor, destructive action or deception was found in the reviewed entrypoint, runtime paths and flagged resources. Model scores were not used as proof.

samples.identification: Static little-endian MIPS O32 flood bot and ELF corruptor
evidence: Rizin: main 0x400498 receives newline-delimited TCP tasks after connecting to embedded host 177.3.213.149. PING replies PONG. UPDATE builds a wget/curl download, chmod and shell-exec command at 0x400d2c-0x400de4.

Task parser 0x400e30-0x4011a8 parses target/port/duration and selects UDP_FLOOD or SYN_FLOOD workers (0x4030e4 and 0x403808); these create packet-sending worker threads, including UDP worker 0x4033b8.
Startup function 0x4018d0 copies the executable into /var/tmp and /usr/lib, applies executable/immutable attributes, and executes generated systemd, cron, rc.local, init.d and shell-profile commands.

At 0x401d64-0x401e18 it walks reboot/shutdown/poweroff/halt paths, opens each for writing, seeks to zero, writes six ELFOOD bytes, and closes it. write wrapper 0x40e230 loads O32 syscall 4004 at 0x40e24c and executes syscall at 0x40e250.
The same startup routine enumerates /proc, resolves executable paths, excludes core-system roots/names, kills selected competitor processes and overwrites/removes their files.
Binary is stripped but not packed. The decoder candidate XOR finding alone is not evidence of intentional obfuscation.

samples.identification: NanoCoreUltimate managed surveillance and disruption program
evidence: ILSpy recovered readable C# without a packing or string-decryption layer. Namespace is NanoCoreUltimate; this does not establish attribution to the commercial NanoCore RAT family.

Main creates hidden/system directories, hides its thread from debuggers, blocks input, disables Defender/security/update services, poisons hosts, deletes shadow copies, writes IFEO hijacks and invokes the fodhelper DelegateExecute UAC-bypass attempt.

InstallPersistence writes its own path to HKCU/HKLM Run keys, copies itself to Startup and creates logon and periodic scheduled tasks. USBWorm copies the running executable to removable drives, hides it and writes AutoRun entries.

StartKeylogger installs WH_KEYBOARD_LL and also polls GetAsyncKeyState, appending keys to a buffer. FlushKeylog encodes the buffer and calls SendToC2. ClipboardMonitor, screenshots and file sweeps likewise record private data.

RecoverBrowserPasswords reads raw Chrome/Edge Login Data and Firefox logins.json, not decrypted passwords. StealBitcoinWallets reads file-valued wallet paths. StealWifiPasswords invokes netsh key=clear and records stdout.

SendToC2 always appends records to Desktop and temp logs first. IsPlaceholder unconditionally returns true and ParseC2Url clears _c2Domain; guarded upload and DNS-beacon branches do not run in this build. Therefore unbound WebClient references cannot prove exfiltration.
AdditionalNetworkBeacon repeatedly calls the same guarded SendToC2. IcmpTunneling separately sends fixed ICMP-TUNNEL-DATA bytes to 8.8.8.8; this is a network operation, not theft of collected input.

RealEncryption enumerates only Desktop/TestFolder and attempts AES->suffixed write->original delete. Its 14-byte AES_IV is invalid for AES, so setting IV throws before output/deletion. Existing trait accurately says replacement attempt.
ProcessHollowing and ProcessInjection use NOP/RET or RET test bytes, not a hidden second payload. DumpLSASS opens the process but does not read/dump its memory.

Independent input surveillance, credential-store copies, security disabling, persistent unauthorized installation and extortion/lockout establish malicious behavior despite broken or placeholder subroutines.
